    A.sort()
    B.sort()
    cnt = 0
    i = 0
    j = 0
    while i < N and j < Q:

            cnt += 1
            i += 1
        j += 1
    return cnt
```

It first sorts both A and B, then uses two pointers, i and j, to iterate through the sorted arrays. If the element at A[i] is less than or equal to the element at B[j], it increments the count and moves the pointer i to the next element in A. Regardless of the comparison result, it always moves the pointer j to the next element in B. This continues until either all elements in A or B have been processed. Finally, it returns the count of elements in A that are less than or equal to the elements in B.
